draft.title: Hypothetical Context Length Increase Causes Slowdown on 16GB GPU - Troubleshooting?
draft.body: I'm investigating a hypothetical slowdown scenario with a local LLM setup. The experiment involves a 16 GB GPU (F1). The issue appears when the context length is increased from 2048 to 8192 tokens (F2). Prior to this change, performance was nominal. Currently, model and runtime versions have not been recorded (F3). We're in the early stages of this hypothetical experiment, so there's no confirmed evidence pointing to driver, system memory, or the model itself being the root cause (F4). Could this be related to how the runtime handles larger contexts, or perhaps an artifact of the hypothetical memory management under these specific conditions? Any pointers on diagnostic steps for this hypothetical scenario would be greatly appreciated.

draft.title: Troubleshooting Hypothetical LLM Slowdown: Context Length Jump on 16GB GPU
draft.body: This is a hypothetical troubleshooting question regarding a local LLM experiment. We're observing a significant slowdown when the context length is increased from 2048 to 8192 tokens (F2). The setup utilizes a 16 GB GPU (F1). It's important to note that this is a hypothetical scenario, and we haven't yet documented the specific model or runtime versions being used (F3). Furthermore, there is currently no evidence to suggest that the issue stems from drivers, system RAM, or a corrupted model file (F4). The slowdown specifically correlates with the context length increase. I'm seeking advice on potential areas to investigate within this hypothetical framework. Could this be related to attention mechanisms, KV cache management, or something else entirely within the inference process when dealing with larger contexts on limited VRAM?
